reviews.title: Beautiful App💗 but accessibility barrier for dyslexia
reviews.body:
I really love using Glorify - the daily devotionals, prayers, and overall design are wonderful for building a regular routine. However, there is a major accessibility issue that needs to be addressed. As someone with dyslexia, reading large blocks of text is a significant barrier, yet the audio-listening feature is locked behind the paid subscription.

While I understand monetizing premium content, basic audio playback is essential assistive technology for neurodivergent and visually impaired users. Connecting with God shouldn't be harder or more expensive just because of a learning disability. I truly hope the developers consider making basic audio narration free so the app can be accessible to everyone in the community.

reviews.title: Use at your risk- Developers are indifferent to issues
reviews.body:
Like everything, this has good and bad elements. The good are the messages, and being able to help others with encouragement and prayer. Though to enjoy the entire app, you have to pay.

The bad are: 
1) Reports of scammers to the Developer, who are blatantly victimizing desperate people , go unheeded. Emails to them go unanswered and people continue to be robbed. Christian sites are prime target for scammers and identity thieves, people are trusting, many are young and too many people believe everyone else there is a Christian with morals. A small group is trying to warn others of the predators, but people still report being victimized. If the developers would ban them, this wouldn't happen. I hope they realize they're liable for failure to act on reports of thieves.

2) There's no instructions on use, rules of conduct, how to report, or repercussions for those who rob or abuse others on this Christian site. 

3) Reports of members posts, who are abusive to others and use profanity, including F bombs, also go unheeded, and they are allowed to continue. Many have left due to how offensive some insist on being and are allowed to continue to. 
It's becoming more like certain social media sites every day, where people forget where they are and why they are there.

4)Too many tech issues! You cannot correct a message to someone or statement, without completely deleting it and starting over. Nor go back to any of your messages or posts easily. I was at the end of answering a persons question, when a pop-up interrupted, telling me an update is available. I refuse to write that message for a third time!  If you run out of alloted characters when pasting scripture to a comment, instead of letting you know, it deletes your entire message and closes the app!! 

5) The NIV Recently removed a verse from Bible. The developers in their lack of wisdom, removed it from every Bible on their site, though they aren't NIV Bibles!!

If you just want to read a quote, some scripture, a devotional that seems to always describe Jesus as cosmic or radical, two of their favorite words, and presumes that everyone has a busy, hectic, strapped for time life (because that's who they speak to the majority of the time ) , and a prayer, then go about your day, this is for you. 

If you want depth of meaning, a closer walk with God, without having to pay for it, to easily contact specific people you want to check on or have over time, developed a relationship with and want to reach them,  to not spend half of your day fighting a system, to wind up giving up out of frustration, look elsewhere, as I've just decided to do.

reviews.title: What Happened?
reviews.body:
Glorify was one of my favorites: I could read AND listen to the Bible verses and devotionals (I have ADD/ADHD, so having something to listen to while I read helps me focus). I loved the courses, the music, everything…until they put it behind a paywall.

Why would you make me pay for something that used to be free? And having to pay for the AUDIO verses and devotionals? What about people who have vision issues or any other impairment that would benefit from using the audio? You’re seriously putting an accessibility feature behind a paywall? That rubs me the wrong way as a consumer who cares about other people and not just myself.

The BIGGEST thing is that it’s sending a message to nonbelievers: The money in your wallet dictates how close you can get to Christ. THIS is why Christianity gets a bad rap. Putting God behind a paywall doesn’t encourage people to seek His face. And I mean, hell, why would I wanna pay for a Bible app when I can just go watch porn for free? MAKE IT MAKE SENSE.

Glorify USED to be my favorite. But now? I’m gonna recommend YouVersion Bible App from Life.Church. It’s more expansive and…ITS FREE.

STAY AWAY FROM GLORIFY

I do know where this began and have sadly watched this happen. Would I pay if it still had the Glorious deep scriptural devotions? In a heartbeat! I will NOT be forced to pay for the level of writing I could write. By the way, the free content compared with the paid subscription, is exactly the same! I have written them after each update, this is not news to them. Each reply is an acknowledgment of what I said and an justification of what they’re doing. I feel they have driven me to a point of bad review by telling me, ‘they will give my suggestion of a family plan to the team.’ And what? Gradually putting me here and inevitably making me pay? For what? Other free Biblical publications start offering MORE if you pay! Not manipulations to pay for LESS! Thank you for making this dishonest decision for me! JC

reviews.body: This app is amazing for daily worship and prayer sessions. I loved listening to the sessions everyday but I am rather disappointed that now I need to pay a subscription fee for worship services that used to be free and available. That’s sucks because that’s not in my budget.🫤
Ads, data stealing, company goes against real Christian values, this app needs to go away. I don't want to hear their ads in my secular podcasts or any other podcasts.

reviews.title: You’ll be paying for everything
reviews.body: I first got Glorify when you could have access to multiple feature but soon enough, I fear some will her to pay just to download this app!! I noticed things slowly being put behind a pay wall and now the last thing that is left free is reading the daily devotional. I loved having it read to me and just meditate on the word. But it’s a luxury now to have this feature. It’s a great app. It’s just disappointing to see how quickly it blew up in popularity and how developers saw that as an opportunity for profit rather than for discipleship. I understand some feature need to be paid for just for sustainability of the app. Great! Make features that warrant payment from users. But soon enough, this app will be a “try free for 7 days”… disappointing
gotta pay now upwards of 70$. shame on you putting a price on faith. this is why druskis skit went viral.

reviews.title: App Update requires payment for basic service (that is required for individuals with disabilities)
reviews.body: I’m honestly very upset. My husband and I use to listen to this app every day together and it was great for our faith. Then glorify updated the app and now you could only listen to the passage and devotion if you pay for it. My husband is dyslexic and I drive us to work so neither of us can listen to it and discuss in our normal morning routine anymore. I understand needing people to pay for an upgrade so the developers can get paid, but there are plenty of other nicer perks people can pay for rather than changing a basic level thing like a listening option. This isn’t ok and it’s certainly not ADA compliant so we will be deleting the app since it’s not usable for us anymore.  Please fix this!!

Wow. Starts hitting you up for subscription costs before you can even see what content they have. Really disappointed. UPDATE: Developer response didn't address what I wrote. Shouldn't be listed as a "free" app when there is zero functionality without a subscription.
